ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening at onboarding and on an ongoing real-time basis of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier / CRF) advisories, the CSSF restricted and sanctioned persons list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions database (including Council Regulation 833/2014 as amended and Council Regulation 765/2006 as amended), the UN Security Council consolidated list (incl. UNSCR 1267/1988, 1718, 2253), and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list where a US nexus exists. PEP status is assessed under Article 3-2 of the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12, requiring enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval for establishing business relations, and determination of source of wealth and source of funds. In addition, where an identified individual is executed to a government-connected role outside the EEA, the enhanced monitoring protocol must be documented in the SARL AML file and reported to the CRF if suspicion arises.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) access portal for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at www.lbr.lu; electronic incorporation filings are submitted via the EGE portal at ege.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script and be linguistically usable in French, German, or Luxembourgish; names originating in non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must comply with Article 172 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, the Law of 25 August 2006 on the RCS, and the Law of 19 December 2002, and must not create confusion with existing registered names, must not be misleading, and must not imply a regulated activity unless the corresponding statutory authorization is held or is being obtained in parallel.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: LUXEMBOURG / LETZEBUERG / LËTZEBUERG / LUXEMBURG (protective token requiring Ministry of Justice authorization)
BANQUE / BANK / BANCAIRE (banking monopoly requiring CSSF authorization under the Law of 5 April 1993)
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE / REASSURANCE (requiring authorization from the Commissariat aux Assurances)
FIDUCAIRE / TRUST (restricted token subject to separate ministerial and disciplinary authorization)
FONDS / FUND (CSSF authorization required for collective investment vehicles)

ELECTRONIC MONEY / E-MONEY / ÉMISSION DE MONNAIE ÉLECTRONIQUE / PAYMENT INSTITUTION / PAIEMENT (CSSF pre-clearance required; the name must reflect the EMI authorization sought under the Law of 26 January 2021 on electronic money)
S.A. / SARL / S.À R.L. / SA / SE (regulated legal-form suffixes that must correspond exactly to the chosen structure and be placed at the end of the name)
GROUP / HOLDING (acceptable only where the actual economic description is accurate; may trigger CSSF holding-company scrutiny)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Following an RCS refusal, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Minister of Justice (Ministère de la Justice, Direction des affaires civiles et commerciales) within one month of the refusal notification, enclosing the refusal decision, a legal memorandum demonstrating conformity with the Law of 25 August 2006 and Article 172 of the Law of 10 August 1915, and any prior authorization letters for sensitive tokens. Where the Minister issues an unfavorable decision, a further annulment action (recours en annulation) may be lodged with the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification. As an alternative, if the rejection is purely formal, the applicant may cure the defect and refile the name for a new 30-day reservation via the EGE portal without prejudice to the existing incorporation timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not permissible for an electronic money institution. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a real head office (siège social) situated in Luxembourg per Article 109 of the Law of 10 August 1915. CSSF prudential doctrine under the Law of 16 March 2018 and the EMI-specific requirements of the Law of 26 January 2021 require effective management, actual decision-making, governance, and business continuity to be anchored in Luxembourg. A registered-address-only arrangement would be rejected during CSSF licensing review and would constitute a material compliance deficiency under CSSF Regulation 12-02.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 710-1 et seq. governing SARL); Law of 10 August 2011 on Electronic Money Institutions; Law of 5 April 1993 on the Financial Sector, as amended (CSSF supervisory powers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed with RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash before notarization; subscription funds must be held in notary escrow until RCS registration. As an electronic money institution, the company is additionally required to maintain minimum own funds of EUR 350,000 at all times under CSSF licensing rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscribers ratify the incorporation of a Luxembourg Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) named LU SARL, authorize the full subscription of the registered share capital in cash, and approve the initial capital placement in escrow pending registration. RESOLVED: that the registered office be adopted at 5 Rue Guillaume, Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED: that Jean Dupont be and is hereby appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole power of representation, and Maria Silva be appointed AML compliance officer. RESOLVED: that the Manager be authorized to complete RCS registration, open a professional bank account, and file all required regulatory applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and notarization of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution or deposit the full capital with the notary's escrow account. Solemnly execute the articles of incorporation before the notary, confirming cash subscription only and the manager's appointment. The notary will confirm legal capacity and that the capital has been irrevocably blocked pending registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copies of subscribers and manager
Proof of full payment of share capital from Luxembourg bank or escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the file, cure the deficiency by correcting the drafts or providing updated identification and financial evidence; re-execute the deed on the same or next working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed and standard RCS registration form via the LBR e-filing system. The RCS verifies the company name, registered office, corporate purpose, and legal form before issuing a registration extract and allocating a Luxembourg registration number.
required_dossiers: RCS Form A (dealing with incorporation details)
Excerpt of deed for RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the notary or legal counsel corrects the filing in the LBR portal within 15 days; any refusal may be challenged by an application to the RCS registrar or, if necessary, before the commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry automatically sends the constitutional extracts to the RESA for mandatory publication. Verify the published extract on the RESA website and retain proof of publication for lender and counterparty due diligence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, submit a correction request to the RCS and Legilux; issue a rectification announcement with court approval if the error affects third-party rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory licensing and commercial establishment permit application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CSSF and Luxembourg Ministry of Economy – Directorate for Business Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic money institution (EMI) licence application with the CSSF using the eDesk channel, including compliance program, operational program, business plan, governance and AML policies, and proof of own funds. Simultaneously submit the business establishment permit application to the Ministry of Economy. No regulated activity may begin before both authorizations are effective.
required_dossiers: Governance and internal control organisational chart
Business establishment permit application and related annexes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to every CSSF query within the stated period; amend the programme or governance arrangements as requested. A final refusal may be appealed before the Luxembourg administrative courts; a materially changed application must be re-filed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Economy – Directorate for Business Establishment (Direction des autorisations d'établissement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business establishment permit (Autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011, complemented by the CSSF electronic money institution licence under the Law of 10 August 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration only; no full EIA report required because the activity is limited to office-based financial technology services with no industrial installation, combustion plant, or significant land disturbance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive 91/271/EEC for sanitary effluent; zero industrial process wastewater or process air emissions; waste handling and disposal in accordance with the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management and EU Regulation 1907/2006 (REACH) insofar as applicable to office consumables.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) for the registered office and any company facilities; structural load and electrical safety inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines for workplace occupancy; occupational health assessment for office employees including emergency evacuation and first-aid arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs and excise; electronic filing and registration portal: myguichet.lu with the eCDF dedicated VAT clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL through the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) (one-stop-shop notary/portal) and obtain the 17-digit national business number (matricule) and RCS identification. Step 2: The RCS matricule triggers automatic tax registration with the ACD and automatic issuance of the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) by the AEDT for resident entities. Step 3: For a non-resident EMI establishing a branch or engaging in taxable Luxembourg supplies, file VAT Form 163 with the AEDT via myguichet.lu, appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative if the EMI has no EU seat or permanent establishment, and obtain an LU-prefixed EORI number through the ADA where any goods flows exist. Step 4: Activate the eCDF/MyGuichet taxpayer account for electronic submission of VAT returns (LTV 500/501), the EC Sales List (Form 600), annual tax declarations for CIT (form 400), and any VAT refund application under the 13th Directive (2003/11/EC) or Directive 2008/9/EC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections. Available statutory elections and regimes: (1) fiscal unity ('intégration fiscale') under Article 164bis LIR for resident Luxembourg subsidiaries held at least 95%, irrevocable for 5 years; (2) VAT grouping allowing a single taxable person ('assujetti unique') under Articles 58-59 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, extending to cross-border permanent establishments; (3) territorial allocation option for Luxembourg permanent establishments of foreign head offices under Article 183bis LIR; (4) participation exemption regime (Articles 147-148 LIR) for dividend and capital gains relief, which is statutory and not elective; (5) advanced binding tax rulings pursuant to Article 29 LIR and circulars (including the Intra-Group Financing, IP, and VAT ruling guidelines) permitting embodiment of the EMI's payment-rail pricing and exempt financial margin treatment. Hybrid mismatch elections are an accepted offensive/mitigative mechanism for Luxembourg hybrid entities only to the extent permitted by the Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (EU) 2016/1164 and the Luxembourg Law of 21 December 2018, primarily through court-tracked misinterpretation avoidance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident small-business exemption threshold: EUR 35,000 taxable turnover per calendar year (Article 57(2) of the Luxembourg VAT Law). Non-EU-established taxable persons benefit from zero de minimis and must telematically register unless their supplies are subject to reverse charge; intra-EU distance sales and TBE-supplied digital services are assessed against the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold under the On-Shore/OSS scheme. Financial and payment services (virtual IBAN, wallet custody, SEPA clearing) are VAT-exempt and, when exclusively performed, do not count toward the registration/taxable turnover threshold; however, any taxable agency, e-identification or consultancy revenue will aggregate for threshold purposes and topple the small-business profit remuneration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance mechanism, digital stamping regime, or mandatory SAF-T for VAT. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies under the Law of 27 June 2018 as implemented through PEPPOL BIS 3.0 (central public procurement portal) effective 1 March 2021. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary on PEPPOL/EN 16931 standards, with mandatory B2B e-invoicing and structured e-reporting expected to be phased in from 2026 under draft Bill 7947. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via eCDF/MyGuichet; for the licensed EMI, VAT filing is generally monthly (standard regime) because its output is dominated by exempt financial services and input VAT deduction is unavailable except for the segregated taxable sleeve, mandating careful proportional deduction and affiliate services invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The EMI's principal services—virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, SEPA credit processing and payment transactions—are VAT-exempt without credit under Article 44 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (implementing Article 135(1)(d) VAT Directive); such exempt financial intermediation is not zero-rated. Zero-rating (0%) is available for: (1) exports of tangible goods from Luxembourg to third-country destinations under Article 56 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, subject to proof of physical departure within 90 days; (2) intra-Community supplies of goods under Article 51 of the Luxembourg VAT Law where the acquirer holds a valid EU VAT number (validated via VIES); and (3) business-to-business services whose place of supply is fixed in a non-EU jurisdiction pursuant to Articles 17 and 20 of the Luxembourg VAT Law—for those offshore services the supply falls outside Luxembourg VAT territorial scope and is effectively zero-rated; the customer's status as a taxable person and its non-EU establishment must be documented contractually and evidenced by its foreign TIN/registration, served through reverse-charge or no-VAT invoicing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) lodged via Luxembourg LU-Export / AES with the ADA for any physical goods movement
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (or CMR for road transport) evidencing physical departure from Luxembourg to a third country
Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the EMI's LU VAT number, the customer's/originator's VAT/TIN, and the exact export reason
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/SEPA payment voucher showing forex repatriation and bank settlement traceability

For offshore services: executed service agreement, IT-systems documentation, customer KYC/AML file, proof of non-EU business establishment (residency certificate or foreign VAT/TIN), and the VIES evidence of the EU customer's VAT status where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ADA perform automated Big Data cross-checks between SAD export declarations, VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and bank payment flows; a false export zero-rating claim or service-supply mischaracterisation triggers full retrospective reversal of the VAT exemption plus the underlying input VAT clawback, monthly statutory late interest, and administrative fines of up to three times the evaded VAT. Where abuse of law (abus de droit) or fraudulent intent is shown under Articles 66 et seq. of the Luxembourg VAT Law and the General Anti-Abuse Rule operating through Article 6 of the Tax Adaptation Law (Steueranpassungsgesetz), the limitation period extends to 10 years, criminal fines of up to EUR 20,000 may be imposed on responsible management, and the directors become joint and severally liable for the reassessed VAT; foreign-exchange manipulation or circumvention of the 180-day repatriation benchmark further exposes the EMI to CSSF supervisory sanctions and revocation of its electronic-money licence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates inside the Economic and Monetary Union with the euro as legal tender; full convertibility applies to both current account and capital account transactions under Articles 63–65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no exchange-control authorizations, surrender requirements, or conversion quotas for cross-border capital movements, profit distributions, dividend remittances, or loan repayments. Any restriction would only arise from EU restrictive measures, UN/EU sanctions, or AML/KYC-related payment blocking, not from foreign exchange regulations. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate law solvency tests, Luxembourg GAAP/IFRS distributable reserves, and withholding tax compliance for outbound dividends, none of which constitute capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export receipts. An entity may hold export proceeds in foreign currency accounts with Luxembourg credit institutions or convert them freely into euro through the interbank market. The only obligations are business-accounting congruence (the export receipt must correspond to a declared commercial invoice), transfer pricing compliance where related parties are involved, and CSSF/BCL AML transaction-reporting duties for cash or high-risk cross-border flows. For an Electronic Money Institution, the safeguarding obligation under the E-Money Directive and Luxembourg law must be maintained in low-risk liquid assets, which in practice requires euro or major foreign currency deposits with authorized credit institutions rather than uncontrolled export receivables.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Treasury and FX Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is High for a Luxembourg-domiciled SARL holding a CSSF-authorized EMI license, because such an entity may join SEPA, hold settlement accounts with the BCL, and access TARGET2 via a sponsoring credit institution. Feasibility is Low to Medium for offshore digital EMIs (for example, UK, Lithuania, or Netherlands license holders) seeking direct Luxembourg clearing access: they may open virtual IBANs and nostro accounts with Luxembourg partner banks, but they cannot obtain BCL settlement membership without a Luxembourg establishment, a passport under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), and full compliance with CSSF outsourcing, safeguarding, and fit-and-proper requirements. Most domestic tier-1 banks limit onboarding of offshore EMIs to 'partner-acceptance' or 'bank-as-a-service' arrangements with restricted transaction velocity and mandatory daily reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions uniformly require at least one authorised director or a formally mandated officer of the SARL to appear physically at the bank's registered office or Luxembourg branch for the final KYC interview. Remote account opening is technically permitted where the bank applies eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signatures, video identification, and CSSF Circular 18/698 due-diligence standards, but in practice tier-1 banks exercise residual discretion and will insist on a physical interview for a High-Risk EMI applicant before activating the escrow account or issuing any virtual IBANs. Non-resident directors may satisfy the physical-presence rule by attending a Luxembourg bank branch or by appearing before a Luxembourg notary who then transmits a notarized mandate and certified identification to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EMI license pending or not yet granted at the time of account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft CSSF license application, detailed business plan with projected transaction volumes, pro-forma balance sheet showing initial capital of not less than EUR 350,000 for the EMI license, certificate of incorporation and articles of association, criminal-record extracts of directors, a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming compatibility of the escrow account with CSSF pre-authorization practice, and a commitment letter to complete the authorization process within a defined milestone timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex UBO chain involving trusts, foundations, or interposed Luxembourg holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart with ownership percentages, Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, notarized passports of all ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-wealth questionnaires with supporting bank statements or valuation reports, corporate tax residence certificates for each intermediate entity, and notarized declarations of ultimate control executed within the preceding three months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected transaction volumes disproportionate to paid-in capital or stated business plan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF-compliant business plan with audited financial projections, defined transaction-monitoring thresholds per client and per day, detailed AML/KYC policies and procedures manual aligned with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, regulatory capital adequacy forecast under the E-Money Directive, and evidence of an appointed AML compliance officer and internal auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or UBOs from FATF grey-listed or high-risk third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file containing independent background checks, corroborated source-of-funds documentation (bank references from regulated institutions, tax returns, audited financial statements), professional or institutional references from law firms and banks in reputable jurisdictions, evidence of local economic substance such as a Luxembourg lease and local AML officer, and a detailed explanation of the commercial rationale for the high-risk connection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR or third-country injections and SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR transfers originating within the EEA. For equity capital, use economic-purpose code such as 'Equity injection / subscription of shares' with the creditor UMR (Unique Mandate Reference) and a structured creditor reference; for loans from shareholders, use a shareholder loan agreement with transfer pricing documentation and a clear repayment schedule to avoid reclassification as equity. The receiving Luxembourg bank will require the underlying corporate resolution, board authorization, and AML source-of-funds declaration before crediting the escrow account; funds must match the constitutional minimum capital (at least EUR 12,000 for an SARL, and EUR 350,000 for an EMI) and must be disclosed to the CSSF under the e-money authorization file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EUR-denominated trade settlements within the EEA, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) through the TARGET2 settlement system via the Luxembourg clearing infrastructure; for non-EEA or non-EUR payments, use SWIFT MT103 with full remittance information and correct ISO 20022 purpose codes. For documentary trade settlements, use Commercial Letters of Credit opened through Luxembourg credit institutions with SWIFT MT700/MT710 issuance and UCP 600 terms. As an EMI, outgoing customer payments must be settled exclusively from safeguarded funds held in separate accounts with a credit institution or in secure liquid assets as required by the E-Money Directive implementation in Luxembourg law; the clearing rail must preserve the funds' segregation and prevent any commingling with the EMI's operational capital.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards denominated in EUR against USD, GBP, CHF, and JPY with a maximum tenor aligned to underlying commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies of restricted markets where delivery is impossible
Cross-currency swaps matching balance-sheet asset-liability tenors
Vanilla FX options for treasury income protection
Forward rate agreements for interest-rate risk on safeguarded cash positions
FX basis swaps executed through regulated Luxembourg or EU counterparties, provided they do not create proprietary trading risk beyond the treasury hedging mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements in Luxembourg GAAP, including balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and, where required, management report and independent auditor's report, filed with the RCS and published in the RESA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; by 31 July where the financial year ends on 31 December. Shareholder approval of the annual accounts must occur within 6 months of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is sanctioned by fines up to EUR 5,000, court-ordered compliance, and publication costs; persistent default after formal notice may trigger dissolution and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation and updated RBE declaration in the event of any share transfer, change of control, or beneficial ownership variation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year in accordance with the LBR/RBE confirmation cycle; material changes must be filed within one month after the company becomes aware of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the RBE Law of 13 January 2019 may result in administrative fines, refusal or restriction of RCS extracts, and criminal sanctions against responsible officers for knowing or negligent false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CSSF reporting package for the licensed e-money institution, comprising audited annual accounts, own-funds and safeguarding report, internal-control report, and AML/CFT compliance reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited annual accounts within six months of the financial year-end; annual prudential and AML/CFT internal-control reports according to CSSF circular deadlines, at least once per calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF may impose fines, issue injunctions, restrict activities, appoint a temporary administrator, and suspend or withdraw the EMI licence; directing officers may also face personal administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. In addition, the CSSF licensing regime requires a mandatory independent statutory audit for an e-money institution irrespective of company size thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial and company registration and annual accounts, as amended. EU-endorsed IFRS may be applied for consolidated accounts; CSSF-regulated e-money institutions apply the CSSF chart of accounts and FINREP/COREP reporting taxonomy for regulatory returns.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% Luxembourg corporate income tax (impot sur le revenu des collectivites) plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus municipal business tax (impot commercial communal); aggregate effective statutory burden in Luxembourg City approximately 24.94%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply to EMIs; preferential mechanisms available: 80% IP box exemption on net qualifying IP/software income (LIR Art. 50bis); participation exemption fully exempting qualifying dividend income and capital gains (at least 10% holding or at least EUR 1.2m acquisition cost held at least 12 months); R&D tax credit and investment tax credit up to 12% on qualifying capital expenditure; notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity (rate set annually by Grand-Ducal regulation)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; no carryback; loss-offset requires continuity of business activity under Luxembourg case law)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (declaration relative a l'impot sur le revenu des collectivites) filed together with Form 1001 (impot commercial communal) via the electronic portal MyGuichet/eCDF of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on 31 May of the calendar year following the tax year; automatic extension to 31 December when filed electronically; further extension of up to 6 months available on reasoned pre-deadline request to the competent local tax office (bureau d'imposition)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared tax period and fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg permanent establishment's book year; non-residents identify the home country RCS/registration number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, RCS number, registered office, principal business activity (ISIC 6619)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident EMIs holding a Luxembourg branch licence, state branch address and RCS number of the Luxembourg registration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference to audited financial statements and basis of accounting; attach annual accounts of the SARL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach permanent establishment accounts reflecting locally allocated e-money float and reserve income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book result before tax in accordance with the approved balance sheet and profit and loss account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only the Luxembourg PE's net profit after cost-apportionment; transfer pricing adjustments must be booked at arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: participation-exempt dividends and capital gains, IP-box exoneration (Art. 50bis LIR)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available if the PE or the head office holds qualifying participations; attach documentation of 12-month holding period

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses reintegrated: taxes, fines, 50% of restaurant/entertainment costs, excessive borrowing costs under thin capitalisation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back same items attributable to the Luxembourg PE at the same rates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base after permanent additions/deductions and offsets of carried-forward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final PE taxable income; treaty allocation of loans, intangibles and treasury functions to the PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, dividend WHT imputation credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident EMIs may only claim credits connected with the Luxembourg PE income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default assessment (taxation d'office) and a surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax; late payment triggers monthly interest of 0.6% on arrears; persistent failure may be sanctioned with fixed daily fines and administrative penalties up to EUR 5,000 (AO Art. 396); wilful non-filing exposes directors to criminal fines and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions of a SARL; 0% withholding to EU parent companies holding at least 10% for 12 months under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; treaty rate typically 5% to 10% (0% to 15% depending on DTA) for non-EU residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The paying SARL applies the reduced or zero rate only after the beneficial owner files Luxembourg direct tax form Modele 22 with the ACD, attaches a valid Tax Residence Certificate covering the dividend payment date, and proves the qualifying participation and 12-month holding period; e-file via MyGuichet; excess WHT repaid via ordinary refund procedure within 6 months
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax for non-resident recipients under domestic law (no interest or royalty WHT for corporations); residual 20% savings withholding may apply only to interest paid to Luxembourg-resident individuals

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Report: MNE groups with consolidated revenue at least EUR 750,000,000. No fixed annual Master File/Local File threshold is yet codified in Luxembourg statute for FY 2024/2025; the ACD may compel OECD-aligned documentation under LIR Art. 56 and Circular LIR 56/1 (2016) regardless of size. From FY 2026 (EU Directive 2024/2810 transposition): Local File required where taxpayer net turnover is at least EUR 50,000,000 and intra-group transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000; Master File required for groups with revenue at least EUR 750,000,000; CbCR notification threshold EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate UAE-style ESR statute exists, but economic substance is imposed via LIR Art. 6/56 (abuse of law), LIR Art. 56bis (GAAR), the principal purpose test under DTAs/MLI and CSSF licensing requirements. An EMI must keep its central administration, board meetings, senior employees, AML/compliance function, e-money float treasury management, IT access and service decision-making in Luxembourg; minimal substance triggers reintegration of profits and loss of treaty protection

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / fraudulent misdeclaration on Form 100
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission or false declaration of taxable income, concealing interest on e-money float reserves, fictitious debt deductions, or abusive use of artificial loss-offset structures through foreign shell vehicles
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default assessment and 10% surcharge; 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; administrative fiscal fines under AO Arts. 396-401; on criminal conviction, fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax fraud penalties and damages; courts may impose travel bans, freezing orders and up to 6 months imprisonment on the responsible manager

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letterbox EMI with nominal office, no resident management or employees, treasury and e-money reserve functions performed outside Luxembourg, financing interposed through transparent holding chains for treaty-shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and disregard of artificial transactions under LIR Art. 56/56bis; upward adjustment of taxable base plus 10% surcharge; denial of dividend WHT relief and treaty benefits under the PPT; EU anti-shell presumption leads to reallocation of income to the ultimate parent state
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The entity's managers/beneficial owners may be assessed for restitution equal to the tax shortfall, prohibited from managing Luxembourg companies, and subjected to exit travel bans during collection proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT breach by licence holder (High-Risk EMI)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform KYC/EDD on virtual IBAN beneficiaries, allowing third-party payments in breach of the e-money limitation of liability, processing transactions of sanctioned entities, or unverified pooled wallet/merchant settlement flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines of up to EUR 2,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover per breach; licence suspension or withdrawal; criminal money-laundering sanctions under Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq. (imprisonment 3 months to 5 years, fine EUR 12,500 to EUR 250,000) in addition to confiscation of criminal proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, executive directors and de facto shadow managers face personal criminal conviction, disqualification from banking/fintech management, pecuniary sanctions up to EUR 250,000, travel bans and asset seizure for serious AML failures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed e-money payment activity (running without CSSF licence)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing electronic money, hosting virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet ecosystem, or processing SEPA Credit for third parties without the required EMI authorisation or after exceeding the activities permitted under ISIC 6619 licence scope
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 (payment services regime); CSSF injunctions to cease activity; restitution of all reserve balances; contracts concluded in breach are voidable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: All directors who directed or tolerated the unlicensed activity are personally liable for losses of customers and creditors, subject to imprisonment up to 5 years, travel bans, freezing of personal assets and exclusion from acting as company officers in Luxembourg
